title: People
goal: Describe what someone is like and what they look like, talk about friends, fiancés and in-laws, gossip a little — using full relative clauses ('the guy whose brother …', 'the place I work in') and 'seems / looks like'.
intro:
Half of all conversation is about other people: who that guy is, whether your new colleague is nice or stuck-up, who got engaged, why two brothers aren't speaking, how your friend's mother-in-law is driving him mad. In the Pashtun world, where families are big and everyone knows everyone, this is doubly true.

In this unit you'll learn words for personality and looks, for friends and in-laws, and two pieces of grammar that make describing people easy: **relative clauses in full** — including the little pronouns Pashto adds inside them ('the girl **whose** brother …' = 'the girl that her brother …') — and **seems / looks like** with ښکارېدل, معلومېدل and ورته.

grammar.title: Relative clauses in full: who, whose, with whom, where
grammar.body:
You met the basic pattern in unit 20: the noun, then **چې**, then a clause that ends with its own verb. چې covers 'who', 'which' and 'that':

هغه هلک **چې** هلته ولاړ دی 'the boy who is standing there'
هغه فلم **چې** موږ وليد 'the film (that) we saw'

The noun is usually marked with **هغه** 'that' or **يو** 'a' in front, so the listener knows a چې-clause is coming.

**The key to fluency: Pashto adds a pronoun inside the clause** wherever English uses 'whose', 'with whom', 'in which', 'to whom'. چې never changes; the clause just says where the person or thing fits, with a clitic or a small pronoun:

• **whose** → چې … **يې**: هغه نجلۍ چې ورور **يې** ډاکټر دی 'the girl whose brother is a doctor' (lit. that her brother is a doctor)
• **with whom** → چې … **ورسره**: هغه سړی چې ما **ورسره** خبرې وکړې 'the man I spoke with'
• **in which / where** → چې … **پکې**: هغه دفتر چې زه **پکې** کار کوم 'the office I work in'
• **on / about whom** → چې … **پرې**: هغه نجلۍ چې ته **پرې** مين يې 'the girl you're in love with'
• **whom** (object, present tense) → چې … **يې**: هغه کس چې زه **يې** پېژنم 'the person I know'

**Inside the clause the normal rules apply** — including the ergative in the past: هغه کتاب چې **تا** راکړ 'the book you gave me' (تا, not ته).

**Without a noun**: **څوک چې** 'whoever, the one who', **څه چې** 'whatever, what', **چېرته چې** 'wherever': څوک چې ښه اخلاق لري، خلک يې خوښوي 'people like someone with good manners'; څه چې غواړې، واخله 'take whatever you want'.

The relative clause can also come **after** the main verb when it's long: هغه سړی ما ته ورته دی **چې** … — both orders are fine in speech.

grammar.title: 'Seems' and 'looks like': ښکارېدل، معلومېدل، ورته
grammar.body:
**ښکارېدل** (unit 13) works like 'to look / seem' + an adjective. It takes the normal present endings, and the adjective agrees with the person:

ستړی **ښکارې** 'you look tired' (to a man) · ستړې **ښکارې** (to a woman)
هغه ځوانه **ښکاري** 'she looks young'
موږ خوشاله **ښکارو** 'we look happy'

With a whole sentence: **ښکاري چې** … 'it looks like …': ښکاري چې ناروغ دی 'it looks like he's ill'.

**داسې ښکاري لکه چې** … 'it looks as if …' for something you're guessing: داسې ښکاري لکه چې ټول ويده دي 'it looks as if everyone's asleep'.

**معلومېږي چې** … 'it seems / apparently …' is for a conclusion you've drawn from what you've seen or heard: معلومېږي چې نن نه راځي 'it seems he's not coming today'. For hearsay use **وايي چې** … 'they say …' (unit 20).

**Looking like someone** (resemblance) is different: **X ته ورته** + 'be': مور ته ورته ده 'she looks like her mother', دا دواړه سره ورته دي 'these two look alike'.

**The trap**: don't translate 'he looks like his father' with ښکاري — that would mean 'he appears to be his father'. Use ورته.

culture: Pashtun families are big and close, and family dynamics are a favourite topic — carefully. Men rarely mention their wives by name in public (they say **د کور خلک** 'the people of the house' or 'the children's mother'), and commenting on the looks of another man's sister, wife or fiancée is a serious insult, so keep descriptions of women to close friends of the same sex. Marriages are still mostly arranged between families, often within the extended family, and an engagement (**کوژده**) can last months or years; 'dating' is discreet, and young people say **ملګرې** or the English 'girlfriend' rather than anything more direct. Cousins on the father's side (**تربور**) are famously rivals as well as allies — the word **تربورولي** 'cousinhood' means rivalry. The mother-in-law (**خواښې**) is the stock figure of jokes. Among friends, **انډيوال** (Afghanistan) and **يار** / **يارا** (Peshawar) are what you call your mates. A Pashtun compliment is often about character, not looks: **ښه اخلاق لري**, **سخي دی**, **زړور دی**; calling someone **کنجوس** or **ټګ** is a real insult, so use them with a smile, or behind their back — which is, of course, **غيبت**.

tip.title: The person who …: noun + چې + clause
tip.body:
- چې = who / which / that, and never changes: هغه هلک **چې** هلته ولاړ دی.
- The clause ends with its own verb, then the main sentence carries on.
- Past tense inside is still ergative: هغه کتاب چې **تا** راکړ.
- No noun? **څوک چې** 'whoever', **څه چې** 'whatever'.

tip.title: Whose, with whom, where: the extra pronoun
tip.body:
- Pashto puts a pronoun **inside** the چې-clause where English says whose / with whom / in which.
- whose → **يې**: هغه نجلۍ چې ورور **يې** پوليس دی.
- with whom → **ورسره** · in which → **پکې** · on/about whom → **پرې**.
- چې itself never changes.

tip.title: Looks, seems, looks like
tip.body:
- Adjective + **ښکاري** 'looks': ستړی **ښکارې** 'you look tired'; the adjective agrees.
- **ښکاري چې** / **معلومېږي چې** + sentence: 'it looks / seems that …'.
- **داسې ښکاري لکه چې** … 'it looks as if …'.
- Resemblance: **X ته ورته** دی 'he looks like X' — not ښکاري.
tip.pattern: adj + ښکاري · X ته ورته دی

sentences.en: It looks like he is ill.

sentences.native: معلومېږي چې نن نه راځي.
sentences.roman: maʿluméẓi che nən na rā́dzi.
sentences.en: It seems he's not coming today.

sentences.native: هغه خپل پلار ته ډېر ورته دی.
sentences.roman: haġá xpəl plār ta ḍer wə́rta day.
sentences.en: He looks a lot like his father.

sentences.native: داسې ښکاري لکه چې ټول ويده دي.
sentences.roman: dā́se ṣkā́ri lə́ka che ṭol widə́ di.
sentences.en: It looks as if everyone's asleep.

sentences.native: عينکې دې نوې دي؟ ښې ښکاري.
sentences.roman: aynáke de náwe di? ṣe ṣkā́ri.
sentences.en: Are your glasses new? They look nice.

sentences.native: قد يې لوړ دی او عينکې لري.
sentences.roman: qad ye lwaṛ day aw aynáke lári.
sentences.en: He's tall and wears glasses.

sentences.native: زما قد لنډ دی، خو ورور مې ډېر اوږد دی.
sentences.roman: zmā qad lanḍ day, xo wror me ḍer uẓd day.
sentences.en: I'm short, but my brother is really tall.

sentences.native: دا زما نامزد دی.
sentences.roman: dā zmā nāmzád day.
sentences.en: This is my fiancé.

sentences.native: نامزده دې څه کار کوي؟
sentences.roman: nāmzáda de tsə kār kawí?
sentences.en: What does your fiancée do?

sentences.native: د کوژدې مېلمستيا کله ده؟
sentences.roman: də kozhdé melmastyā́ kə́la da?
sentences.en: When's the engagement party?

sentences.native: زما ورور په يوه نجلۍ مين دی.
sentences.roman: zmā wror pə yawa njlə́y mayán day.
sentences.en: My brother is in love with a girl.

sentences.native: هغه نجلۍ چې ته پرې مين يې، څوک ده؟
sentences.roman: haġá njlə́y che tə pre mayán ye, tsok da?
sentences.en: Who's the girl you're in love with?

sentences.native: خسر مې ډېر مهربان سړی دی.
sentences.roman: xusár me ḍer mehrabā́n saṛáy day.
sentences.en: My father-in-law is a really kind man.

sentences.native: خواښې مې هره ورځ زنګ وهي.
sentences.roman: xwā́ṣe me hára wradz zang wahí.
sentences.en: My mother-in-law phones every day.

sentences.native: مور يې دا واده نه مني.
sentences.roman: mor ye dā wādə́ na mani.
sentences.en: His mother won't accept this marriage.

sentences.native: کوژده يې ماته شوه.
sentences.roman: kozhdá ye mā́ta shwa.
sentences.en: Their engagement was broken off.

sentences.native: مبارک شه! واده مو کله دی؟
sentences.roman: mubā́rak sha! wādə́ mo kə́la day?
sentences.en: Congratulations! When's the wedding?

lessons.title: Fights and gossip
new: زه او هغه سره نه جوړېږو.

sentences.native: دا دوه ورونه تل سره جنګېږي.
sentences.roman: dā dwa wrúna tal sara jangéẓi.
sentences.en: These two brothers are always fighting.

sentences.native: پرون له خپل ورور سره وجنګېدم.
sentences.roman: parún la xpəl wror sara wə́jangedəm.
sentences.en: I had a fight with my brother yesterday.

sentences.native: مه جنګېږئ، ورونه ياست!
sentences.roman: ma jangéẓəy, wrúna yāst!
sentences.en: Stop fighting, you're brothers!

sentences.native: خير دی، سبا به بيا ملګري شئ.
sentences.roman: xayr day, sabā́ ba biyā́ malgə́ri shəy.
sentences.en: Never mind, you'll be friends again tomorrow.

sentences.native: وايي چې د احمد کوژده ماته شوه.
sentences.roman: wā́yi che də ahmád kozhdá mā́ta shwa.
sentences.en: They say Ahmad's engagement is off.

sentences.native: دا رښتيا ده که غيبت؟
sentences.roman: dā rəṣtyā́ da ka ġibát?
sentences.en: Is that true or just gossip?

sentences.native: د خلکو غيبت مه کوه، ښه کار نه دی.
sentences.roman: də xálko ġibát ma kawa, ṣə kār na day.
sentences.en: Don't talk about people behind their backs, it's not nice.

sentences.native: چا درته وويل؟
sentences.roman: chā dərta wə́wayəl?
sentences.en: Who told you?

sentences.native: زما خواښې او زما مور سره نه جوړېږي.
sentences.roman: zmā xwā́ṣe aw zmā mor sara na joṛéẓi.
sentences.en: My mother-in-law and my mum don't get along.

sentences.native: هغوی دواړه سره ښه جوړېږي.
sentences.roman: haġwí dwā́ṛa sara ṣə joṛéẓi.
sentences.en: The two of them get on well.
